context.description: Three worker failures in a row fail the unit with a harness error

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review at HEAD 5fb09be29c (after D8/D9 fixes 077320f8e4, c8ffccfee1); test file unchanged since 6841bc0e5d; trial bun test 3 pass 0 fail. Given a task supervisor whose worker fails: test 1 starts the real TaskSupervisor.machine for the ready leaf T1.1 (asserts tag ready) on a SimulatedClock, with a root directory that has no git repository, so the real begin worker fails on git worktree prune (no worker stand-in; only the session boundary is scripted). When it fails three times in a row: asserts context.failures 1 then 2 in state retrying, nothing stored after failures 1 and 2, no retry at 999 ms and a retry at 1000 ms. Then task.failed with harness error: asserts exactly one stored fact {type task.failed, task T1.1}, reason.startsWith('harness error:') and carries the git error, the supervisor goes quiet with failures 3, T1.1 folds to failed in the real run actor, and no fourth try after 5 s. And a scenario batch records its fact the same way: test 2 runs the real RunSupervisor with S1 ready (asserted via readyScenarios), the real scenarioProof batch fails three times (batchFailures 1, 2 with nothing stored), then exactly one scenario.proved {id S1, status failed} whose reason starts 'harness error:' and S1 folds to failed, no fourth batch. Test 3 adds the scenario supervisor judge path: three claim failures give scenario.verified rejected 'harness error: the session index is closed', no prompt, S2 folds to rejected. Every step has a specific assertion on the real code; no over-mocking of the unit under test.
